## Interpretation guidance

- VHT 2.0 uses the `vhc2` command and is the documented Docker-native workflow for new development.
- VHT 1.x uses the `vhc` command and remains available for existing applications that have not migrated.
- VeeaONE Runtime runs on the target. VHT runs on the developer host and deploys applications to the target.
- Runtime capabilities vary by hardware target. Consult the supported-platform and capability-profile pages before drawing production conclusions.
- Treat exact software versions, supported targets, registry behavior, and production constraints as version-specific. Prefer the corresponding reference page over general summaries.

## Current support boundary

- Supported third-party x86-64 targets currently use Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS. Physical systems and virtual machines are documented.
- Supported NVIDIA targets currently use Jetson Orin hardware with JetPack 6.2.1. Consult the supported-platform page for the tested device list.
- VHT 2.0 runs on an Ubuntu 24.04 LTS developer host and uses Docker-native workflows to deploy to prepared targets.
- Do not infer support for every Arm system, operating system, accelerator, carrier board, or deployment topology from the general runtime-target model.
- This documentation does not by itself grant production access or certify a proposed deployment. Third-party runtime enablement, VeeaCloud services, support, and production use depend on an approved account, supported configuration, and applicable Veea agreement.
